rows.back_translation: As dawn breaks, Lake Tana awakens in silence. Ethiopia's largest lake, the source of the Nile.
For ages, tankwa paddlers have lived traveling on this water. The lake is both their road and their dwelling.
But amidst the forests of the islands, ancient monasteries with a history spanning ages are hidden.
On their walls, saints are seen in colorful paintings. Each painting is both a prayer and a lesson.
Books written on parchment have preserved ancient knowledge and faith for ages.
By taper light, scribes wrote letter by letter on parchment. Their patience is visible even today.
In times of war and hardship, these relics were preserved inside the islands. Even the waves could not destroy them.
Today this trust is in our hands. Knowing, honoring, and protecting it is our responsibility.
Tana is not just a beautiful lake. It is a history not destroyed by waves, so let us protect it for the coming generation.
